newsitem.title: TANZANIA: First joint U.N. trial for Rwanda genocide starts.
newsitem.headline: First joint U.N. trial for Rwanda genocide starts.

text.p: The first joint trial of two Rwandans accused of genocide and crimes against humanity opened on Friday at the International Criminal Tribunal on Rwanda.
Clement Kayishema and Obed Ruzindana pleaded not guilty in the tribunal court in the northern Tanzanian town of Arusha and pointed out mistakes on their background in their indictments.
Kayishema said the prosecution indictment had his parents' names wrong while Ruzindana said he was born in 1962, not 1959.
"Since we are here to establish the truth, the tribunal should recognise the changes," said prosecutor Jonah Rahetlah.
He said he would prove Kayishema was a powerful man at the time of the genocide in Rwanda as prefect of the western district of Kibuye and used his authority to trigger killings.
He said he would prove Ruzindana had social and political power at the time of the genocide and took part in massacres.

The first prosecution witness, Dutch policeman Sjoukes Ekma, presented videotapes, slides and maps of four alleged massacre sites during the genocide in 1994 of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu political moderates by troops, militiamen and mobs.
Under tribunal rules, the accused face life imprisonment if found guilty. Special tribunals for genocide suspects inside Rwanda since December have sentenced at least 18 people to death.

U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan dismissed two top tribunal officials in January after a U.N. report detailed administrative mismanagement, unqualified staff and legal chaos at the tribunal in Arusha.
